- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via os migrate audit-metadata-bodies (command, read off packages/cli/src/commands/migrate/audit-metadata-bodies.ts))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **37** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1e4656d01fe485935c493a00ecdb8e0f8a0fed55` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c921368f22627666263b61209f7eac730ad7479c` — the merge of head `9f6f950f35e63373def1d330eaa5acc0a166b681` into base `1e4656d01fe485935c493a00ecdb8e0f8a0fed55`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c921368f22627666263b61209f7eac730ad7479c && git checkout c921368f22627666263b61209f7eac730ad7479c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1e4656d01fe485935c493a00ecdb8e0f8a0fed55 9f6f950f35e63373def1d330eaa5acc0a166b681 && git checkout -B drift-repro 1e4656d01fe485935c493a00ecdb8e0f8a0fed55 && git merge --no-ff 9f6f950f35e63373def1d330eaa5acc0a166b681

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1e4656d01fe485935c493a00ecdb8e0f8a0fed55
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 1e4656d01fe485935c493a00ecdb8e0f8a0fed55` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对

**L1 verdict: ACCEPT** · PR #34569 · card #34519 · first review · read 2026-11-17T01:56Z

Head-sha: `9f6f950f35e63373def1d330eaa5acc0a166b681` (the head named in final-head comment 6935487847)

Read from GitHub at this head (`get_files`, diff, check-runs), not from the report.

**Checklist**
- Shape: draft, base `main`. The body opens with the attribution lines and then `Fixes #34519`, and the whole card is delivered. #34495 and #34280 appear in the body without a closing verb next to them.
- Scope: 9 files: `cli/src/utils/audit-redaction-seal.ts` (`hostSeam`, async `seal`), one line in each of the four `migrate/audit-*` commands, a new unit pin, one added case in the existing contract test, `content/docs/deployment/cli.mdx`, and a root changeset. No `content/docs/releases/`. Declared deviation accepted: the sink slot is covered beside the signer. It is the same helper and the same fault shape, and leaving it on the catch-all would keep half the defect.
- Changeset: root, patch for `@objectstack/cli` (published). I checked each sentence against the diff:
  - "through a helper that turned every resolution error into 'not registered'" matches `main`'s removed `service()` with a bare `catch`.
  - "A signer registered as a factory was never built at all" matches the old sync `getService`; `hostSeam` now uses `getServiceAsync`.
  - "No host signer registered still amends under the local key, and no sink exports nothing, as before" matches `amendment-writer.ts:391` (`this.seal.signer ?? new LocalCheckpointSigner(…)`) and `:429` (`this.seal.sink?.deliver`).
  - "stops the run before any row is amended or rewritten: it prints … and exits 1" holds: in each command the `await redaction.seal(...)` sits inside the `try` whose `catch` prints `error.message` (or the `--json` error) and calls `this.exit(1)`, and it comes before `underAuditSealLock(`. The new contract case pins both facts per file.
- Docs, `deployment/cli.mdx` (Sealed audit rows), sentence by sentence:
  - "signed by the host's checkpoint signer when the host registers one, and by the deployment's local key when it registers none" is true (`amendment-writer.ts:391`).
  - "a host checkpoint sink … is handed each amendment" is true (`:429`, `kind: 'amendment'`).
  - "A signer or sink that is registered but cannot be resolved stops the run before any row is amended or rewritten: it prints `Audit redaction seal: the '<slot>' service is registered but could not be resolved (<cause>)` and exits `1`" is true: the printed message starts with exactly that text, and the exit is as above.
  - "It never falls back to the local key in place of the host's signer" is true, because only `isServiceNotRegisteredError` maps to `undefined`.
- Tests: the new `audit-redaction-seal.host-seam-34519.test.ts` runs on a real `ObjectKernel` registry with four cases: nothing registered, a throwing signer factory, a throwing sink factory, and a resolving factory signer. The report records 7 ablation reds.
- Gates: 57 check-runs on this head, all `completed`: 40 `success`, 17 `skipped`, 0 failed. Lint & Repo Gates `success`, TypeScript Type Check `success`, Test Core `success`, Check Changeset `success`.

**Spot checks (mine)**
1. The rule and its wording match #34495 (the sealer, `audit-plugin.ts` `hostSeamResolver`). Same branded-error discrimination and same sync fallback for a kernel with no async accessor, so the sealer and the CLI amendment path cannot drift on what "not registered" means.
2. The error keeps the original with `{ cause: error }`, and the slot is named in the message, so an operator sees which registration to fix.
3. A dry run now also stops on an unresolvable host signer, because `seal()` is awaited before the dry/apply split. That is the conservative direction (a dry run would otherwise report decisions a real run cannot make) and needs no change.

**L2 owed: no.** None of the four contract faces is touched: `Clause-②: no`, no narrowing, no `packages/spec/src/**` path, no governed rule text. `RedactionSealRun` is a CLI-internal util type and the CLI exports no library surface.

**Landing tier**: `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 34569` reports NOT governed, +174/−16 = 190 lines ≤ 3000. Ordinary queue landing by the area at this head. This closes the same-family follow-up named in my ACCEPT on #34495.
